rows.name: Valtay Corporation
rows.blurb: They keep the best of you alive. A corpse that sits up is retention.
rows.invite_pitch: You went down in a fight. They want the corpse that sits up.
rows.task_teaser: Before a boss fight, on camera, talk the boss into a numbered employment contract.
rows.gift_effect: Wear it. The first blow that lands puts two points back. Twist it once, close 1d6, and you knit for ten minutes. Then the ring is spent.

rows.name: Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network
rows.blurb: A charity, for broadcast purposes. They love a death with clean hands.
rows.invite_pitch: You played the evening and never drew blood. The booth opens.
rows.task_teaser: Reach the stairs having dealt no damage to a living creature the whole floor.
rows.gift_effect: A cloak of clean hands. It turns one point of every blow, and the first three hits each leave a two-point guard on the blow after.

rows.name: Veriluxx RealPet Companions
rows.blurb: A pet company. The pet is the client. The crawler is the hands.
rows.invite_pitch: You gave something away and drew no blood. They have a collar.
rows.task_teaser: Adopt a living mob, name it on camera, and walk it to the stairs alive.
rows.gift_effect: Clipped on the pet. Once, it steps in front of a blow and takes two points of it.

rows.name: Jaxbrin Amusements, Limited
rows.blurb: Pull the tag. Ages three and up. The figure may retain opinions.
rows.invite_pitch: A natural twenty in a fight. They want that face on the box.
rows.task_teaser: In a boss fight, read the full hang-tag out loud — name, ages, warning — then throw the figure.
rows.gift_effect: Blow it. For three rounds blows have trouble finding you, and nothing can grab you or slow you. Then it is spent.

rows.name: Squim Conglomerate
rows.blurb: The floor is ore. One of you is the product. They pay the champion.
rows.invite_pitch: Three different things came off the floor with you. They want a weight.
rows.task_teaser: Strip a room to fixtures, weigh them for the lens, and name one champion out loud.
rows.gift_effect: The bag holds a room of torn-out fixtures. It pads one point of a blow, and the first three times someone in arm's reach hits you, a splinter bites them for one.

rows.name: B.U.T.T.O.N
rows.blurb: Ballistic Utility & Tactical Triggered Ordnance Network. Powerful, uncontrollable effects on activation.
rows.invite_pitch: You fumbled your own roll in a fight. They love blind fire.
rows.task_teaser: Fire a weapon you have never practised, blind, into a fight you did not start, and have it be the shot that ends the scene.
rows.gift_effect: Press it. You hit harder for two rounds, and a fuse starts in you. When the fuse ends it burns for 1d4 unless something puts it out. It cannot do what you asked for.

rows.name: C.H.A.O.S.
rows.blurb: Chaotic Hazard Allocation & Outcome Systems. Combat, stats and abilities come out scrambled.
rows.invite_pitch: Five rolls you made yourself. They want both faces on the reel.
rows.task_teaser: Win a fight in which every attack roll at the table was made with someone else's dice, and you suggested it.
rows.gift_effect: Spend it. The next check is easier, and the one after is harder. You do not pick the face.

rows.name: Church of the Mad Llama
rows.blurb: Waiting on the Great Spit. They fund chaos that does not harm cameloids.
rows.invite_pitch: An effect landed on you, and no cameloid took a scratch.
rows.task_teaser: Cause a scene the AI replays twice, without a llama, alpaca or related creature taking a single point of damage.
rows.gift_effect: One spit, in a fight. Hit, and it burns one of them for 1d4 while blows look past you. Miss, and the smell stays on you.

rows.name: Cogsworth & Sons Automata Co.
rows.blurb: Robots for industry and combat. Overconfident. Occasionally unionising.
rows.invite_pitch: You flipped a mechanism yourself. A shop steward is on the way.
rows.task_teaser: Talk a construct or machine into refusing an order from its owner, on camera.
rows.gift_effect: Carry it and the first three spells you land sharpen the next page or mechanism you study. Wind it once and your voice carries for ten minutes, then the key is spent.

rows.name: Colossus Armory
rows.blurb: Armour that turns a last stand into a drawn-out inconvenience.
rows.invite_pitch: Heavy plate took a real hit and you were still standing.
rows.task_teaser: Stay on your feet for a full round after you should have dropped, wearing armour that is already broken.
rows.gift_effect: Heavy plate. It turns two points of a blow. The first one that gets through leaves 1d6 temporary hits for three rounds.

rows.name: Dilbert's Incredible Chaos Katanas
rows.blurb: Standard to enchanted chaos katanas. The marketing is not subtle.
rows.invite_pitch: You killed with a weapon in your hands. Name the blade next time.
rows.task_teaser: Kill something with a blade you named out loud, using a slogan from their advert, without laughing.
rows.gift_effect: A tiny katana. Its first three cuts leave the target brittle, so the next physical hit bites for two more.

rows.name: EnnerGeX
rows.blurb: Inner-system energy corp, harvesting a red dwarf. Deep pockets. Several crawlers a season.
rows.invite_pitch: You burned and you were still walking. They want the conduit.
rows.task_teaser: Channel a lethal electrical or fire effect through your own body and still be the one who walks away.
rows.gift_effect: A marble of starfire. Thrown, it burns, and the first hit leaves a fuse that goes off for 1d4 fire unless something puts it out.

rows.name: GigaChad Energy Drinks
rows.blurb: Hyper-masculine energy drinks. They rarely sponsor anyone who is not performing the bit.
rows.invite_pitch: You landed a heavy blow in a fight. Flex before it wears off.
rows.task_teaser: Chug something that should have killed you, flex for the lens, and win the next exchange before it wears off.
rows.gift_effect: One can. Three rounds where you hit harder, then you stun out for a round. The crash is the spot.

rows.name: Pettigrew & Collar
rows.blurb: Couture for the lens. One crawler, in the frock they sent, collared, and not consulted.
rows.invite_pitch: You dressed yourself. They would like to do it properly.
rows.task_teaser: Sit in Miss Hem's chair and let her dress you.
rows.gift_effect: A chrome collar with a blinking Pettigrew & Collar logo. Locked. The remote is not on it. --- Locked while anyone holds Hem's Remote.

rows.name: Invictus Corp
rows.blurb: Performance gear. Nanite outfits that demand constant food and water.
rows.invite_pitch: You passed two checks and never drank a potion. The kit approves.
rows.task_teaser: Finish a chase or a fight in their kit without eating or drinking, then collapse on camera the moment it ends.
rows.gift_effect: Once. It clears exhaustion and steadies the next climb. Do not eat yet.

rows.name: M.O.I.S.T.
rows.blurb: Multiphase Organic Irrigation & Sustainment Technologies. Hydration as healing.
rows.invite_pitch: You took a hit and you did not drink a potion.
rows.task_teaser: End a fight that should have needed a potion, having healed only with water you found down here.
rows.gift_effect: It refills. A drink closes 1d4 and puts out fire and fuses. It tastes like the last place you almost died.

rows.name: S.P.L.O.O.G.E
rows.blurb: Strategic Performance Logistics & Overclocking Optimization Group Enterprise. Short, extreme spikes.
rows.invite_pitch: You failed a check you made yourself. They sell the spike that follows.
rows.task_teaser: Break your own limit on camera — a check you had no business passing — and be useless for the rest of the scene.
rows.gift_effect: Once. Two rounds of overclock, then a round of exhaustion. Don't mix them up.

rows.name: The Crawler Memorial Project
rows.blurb: A non-profit, supposedly. They collect crawler stats for a sister company that prints trading cards.
rows.invite_pitch: You went down outside a fight. They already printed the wrong stats.
rows.task_teaser: Die on camera, come back, and read your own memorial card out loud without changing a word they wrote.
rows.gift_effect: A card with your face. Read it for 1d6 temporary hits for an hour, and your next blow that draws blood puts up to two points back. The stats were wrong.
